smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring moves methods into mixins but does not remove them from the mandatory base interface - ParamType still inherits from all three mixins, forcing all subclasses to carry the same baggage. The interface segregation smell persists almost entirely unchanged.

cross_file_coordination.justification: The diff only shows changes to types.py with no corresponding updates to core.py where Parameter.process_value() calls validate_constraints (lines 2434-2438) and deprecation logic calls resolve_value_source (lines 2571-2589). The invocation sites that force these methods to matter are untouched, leaving the smell fully active.

structural_soundness.justification: While creating mixins demonstrates awareness of separation of concerns, making ParamType inherit from all three mixins defeats the purpose. The structure is actually worse because it adds complexity (three new classes) without achieving segregation. resolve_value_source remains oddly placed directly on ParamType instead of being moved to a mixin.

code_quality.justification: The mixin classes are reasonably well-documented and implement their methods correctly. However, the pattern creates confusion - why extract mixins if every type still inherits all of them? The Choice class now redundantly lists all three mixins when it already gets them from ParamType. resolve_value_source is inconsistently handled.

interface_decomposition.justification: Methods are extracted into separate mixin classes (ShellCompletionParamTypeMixin, ConstraintValidationParamTypeMixin, DiagnosticInfoParamTypeMixin) but ParamType immediately inherits all three, making the decomposition purely nominal. No actual segregation occurs.

split_quality.justification: The split creates the appearance of segregation but is completely ineffective. Path still inherits validate_constraints even though it only contains a no-op. All types still carry diagnostic and value-source methods regardless of need. The granularity is correct but the application is wrong.

interface_segregation_resolution.justification: While the three problematic methods are factored into mixins (good instinct), ParamType inherits from all three mixins on line 319, meaning every subclass still gets all methods by default. Types like Path, String, Int etc. are still forced to inherit validate_constraints, get_diagnostic_info, and resolve_value_source. The forced dependency is unchanged - this is reorganization, not segregation. resolve_value_source isn't even in a mixin.

concern_separation_and_coupling_reductio.justification: The mixins demonstrate awareness of the three distinct concerns (validation, diagnostics, value-source), but coupling is not reduced. Core.py invocation sites are unchanged (no diff shows Parameter modifications), meaning the implicit contracts remain. Context metadata coupling persists. Choice explicitly re-lists all three mixins (lines 337-341) when it shouldn't need to if proper segregation existed. Only superficial concern grouping achieved.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring creates the superficial appearance of interface segregation by extracting mixins, but immediately undermines it by making ParamType inherit from all three mixins. Every subclass still carries all methods, no-op implementations like Path.validate_constraints remain necessary, and the core.py invocation sites that force these dependencies are not modified. The smell is reorganized but not eliminated.
